1.html:
Fly over them, we need to have a clear line of sight !
The officer was standing in the opening of the ship making a large turn, enabling him to look at the target with a clear view. They were five of them, medium size war aircrafts, circling around the enemy, with excitement, but also a deep fear of misunderstanding the situation.
All dressed in black, a helmet with a HUD giving him live data, the officer was analysing the huge targets below them.
...
King Class Cruiser.
No Turrets.
No Ionics.
Radioactive materials - low (Level 5 - deep space travels radiations)
Apotium detection - low (Level 5 - deep space travels dust)
Unidentified elements in core.
Several human life forms in core.
Organic materials 99.5%.
Origine...
Origine...
Origine...
...
- G¤d D@mmit, what the hell is this lieutenant ?
- No time to ask, load the rapid canons and arm missiles !
The five medium size ships, while continuing a fast and large circle maneuver around the huge organic beasts, communicated with the atmospheric missile defenses and planetary counter-invasion protocols. The sky was about to become a huge nightmare for those trespassers from outer space.
Standing in the opening of the ship, holding himself to a metal barre usually used for the paratroopers, the officer was pointing at the head of the beasts, the weight of responsibilities standing on his shoulders, however dreams of glory and victory in this instance.
There was no way the invaders would survive the power unleashed by their batteries.
He gave the order, yelling inside the ship to cover the wind blowing and shouting.
The ships opened fire, rapid canons flanking the hull, delivering massive armor piercing rounds every second in a massive hell fire. The pilots had to stabilise the ships in the circling as the feedback was huge.
From above, dispersing the clouds in its trajectory, flaming missiles went straight down onto the enemy while thousands of flashes appeared everywhere beneath them as the planetary Anti Aircraft Artillery was joining the fray.
Explosions were so intense that the heath and bright light of the fireballs were blinding the circling ships. As the flames were getting dangerously close to them and the officer asked the pilots to disengage to gain some distance while the fury did its bidding.
And within seconds of the ships flying away, the officer renewed his position in the opening, looking behind the ship at the disappearance of the fire and black smoke taken by the wind expecting dust, blood and carcasses to fall into the ocean beneath. However he discovered in astonishment that the huge beasts, those beetle like monsters were still flying with very little damage received, one glowing, a kind of darkness within.
